summary: The classic Supermicro BMC web interface: one POST form on the controller's own origin whose fields are named name and pwd and which posts to /cgi/login.cgi. The newer Redfish-era interface is not covered.

sources.title: A third-party imitation of the Supermicro BMC login page: the only markup found
sources.note: Not the vendor's page: a hobby project of 2024 that mimics it. Its form name, field names and submit input agree with the two wire-level sources; its form action is empty. Which board or firmware it was modelled on is not stated.

sources.title: Cloudpods BMC console helper for Supermicro: the HTML login is a form post of the fields name and pwd to /cgi/login.cgi
sources.note: Wire level only: it shows the request, not the page. The Referer it sends is the root page.

sources.title: Public login-request template for the Supermicro BMC: the same two field names and the same path
sources.note: Read for the request shape only. Wire level, no markup.

selectors.note: The field name is also the one the two wire-level sources post.
The field name is also the one the two wire-level sources post.

fixtures.note: The form of the imitation with the action of the wire-level sources. Without the imitation's script, inline handler, layout table and image.

unverified: The markup as a whole: it is taken from an imitation of the page, supported only by two tools that post the same field names. No vendor page or source was read.
Which boards and firmware serve this form. Nothing read names a generation; the newer Redfish-era interface of current boards was not found in any public source and is not covered.
The submit control and the page path. The steps carry no path gate.
Directory sign-in (Active Directory, LDAP, RADIUS) and any second factor: nothing about them was read.
neededFromUser: The login page of your BMC saved as "Webpage, Complete", with the board model and BMC firmware version. One successful sign-in with this layout would also confirm it. Save any page signed out and with no password typed in; keep the "_files" folder beside the .html and both outside the repository: they can hold the account name.
notes: A public repository titled as Supermicro IPMI firmware source code exists (devicenull/supermicro_ipmi_firmware). It was not opened: firmware is outside what this review may read.
